summary.text: A 35-year-old woman was admitted in January 2014 with an over 20-year history of recurrent generalized tonic‒clonic seizures and psychiatric symptoms and 1 + month of recurrence; similar episodes in 1991, 1996, 1999, 2002 and 2008 each recovered after short-term glucocorticoid therapy, and she had taken sodium valproate for 6 years without seizures. After admission levetiracetam did not control seizures, and she developed status epilepticus with autonomic features and hypoventilation requiring breathing support, and was treated in the ICU.

CSF showed leucocytosis and elevated protein with negative viral testing, brain MRI was normal, EEG showed diffuse slow waves, and whole-body CT showed no tumor. CSF and serum were positive for anti-NMDAR antibodies, so anti-NMDAR encephalitis was diagnosed and she received IVIG and glucocorticoids, recovering after 6 months and then taking levetiracetam and azathioprine.

In February 2020 she was readmitted with a seizure attack and, despite IVIG and pulse glucocorticoids, had cluster seizures and status epilepticus and was transferred to the ICU. CSF showed pleocytosis, antibodies were not detected, chest and abdominal CT showed no tumors, and brain MRI and EEG were normal. She was given levetiracetam, diazepam and midazolam, gradually recovered, and was prescribed mycophenolate and levetiracetam after discharge.

In October 2022 she was readmitted with a seizure attack; EEG and CSF were normal and antibodies were negative, but brain MRI showed suspicious bilateral hippocampal hyperintensity. She had no psychiatric symptoms or further seizure, was given levetiracetam and was discharged after 10 days on levetiracetam and mycophenolate mofetil. The authors describe progression to autoimmune-associated epilepsy.
